claims.text: Regular 16-bit finetuning of LLaMA 65B needs more than 780 GB of GPU memory
claims.ours: 783 GB at 12 bytes per parameter (BF16 weights and gradients, FP32 Adam moments); 1045 GB at 16 bytes
claims.how: parameters 65,285,660,672 x bytes; the paper gives no accounting, and 12 bytes is the one that lands just above 780

claims.text: Double quantisation cuts the constants from 0.5 to 0.127 bits per parameter (0.373 saved)
which saves about 3 GB on a 65B model
claims.ours: 3.04 GB (all 65,285,660,672 parameters); 3.02 GB counting only the quantised linear weights
claims.how: 0.373 bits x parameters / 8

claims.text: Figure 6 adapter memory (r = 64 on every linear layer, BF16)
claims.ours: 320 / 501 / 975 / 1599 MB by recount
claims.how: every printed label is exactly 0.90 of the recount (0.901, 0.899, 0.900, 0.901); the optimizer label is exactly 4 x the adapter label (8 bytes per parameter for 32-bit Adam against 2 for BF16), so the labels share one count, 10% below r = 64 on all seven matrices

claims.text: Figure 6 model memory (the 4-bit base)
claims.ours: 3866 / 7201 / 17414 / 34459 MB for NF4 + DQ weights with 16-bit embeddings, head and norms
claims.how: the printed values are 1,000 to 1,900 MB above a weights-only recount; the paper does not say what else the bar holds (the CUDA context and buffers are likely), and §2 and Figure 6 differ by 2 MB for the same 7B model

claims.text: LoRA weights equal to 0.2% of LLaMA 7B take 26 MB

claims.text: 65B finetuning fits in under 48 GB
